title: Minimax Transported Effect Estimation When the Target Observes Only a Covariate Subset
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision PASS; novelty subfield with score ceiling 7.3 below field floor 7.4, salvageable=false and no bounded improvement directive.
gap_reasons: The slow converse is witnessed entirely inside the no-shift submodel with uniform target density, so it establishes the ambient worst-case rate but does not show that partial-covariate transport, population shift, or vanishing target density creates additional hardness.
The result remains restricted to scalar V and W, comparable sample sizes, known smoothness, and point estimation without adaptation, confidence procedures, or asymptotic distribution theory.

The claimed relevance to the nuMoM2b-to-NSFG analysis is not supported by an implementation, computation, or application under that study's higher-dimensional and survey-weighted design, which limits the completed package's leading-journal significance.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the seven-measure cubic estimator, finite-sample variance and cancellation argument, and matched scalar common-smoothness minimax rate; D0.5 math and decision panels passed. The field novelty claim fell to subfield because the lower bound is inherited from a no-shift source-ATE submodel and the fixed-count scalar result does not establish the broader transport or application claims. Formalization reached a compiling declaration scaffold with existing sorry proofs; the unequal-smoothness frontier remains open.
tldr: For two independent fixed-count samples in which the source observes continuous \(V,W,A,Y\) and the target observes only continuous \(V\), the minimax root mean squared error is \(n^{-1/2}\vee n^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), with the elbow at \(\beta=1/2\). The model imposes no positive lower bound on the target density: \(g\) may vanish, while its upper bound follows from the common Holder ball. The constructive contribution is an observable seven-measure split-histogram estimator with separate quadratic and cubic resolutions and a finite-sample cubic variance and cancellation lemma. The slow converse is inherited from an embedded no-shift source-average-treatment-effect sign mixture. The separately defined anchor-faithful fixed-count subclass has the same rate, with a direct witness converse. No equality with the published \(V=X\) mixture-sampling class is claimed.
gap: Published global minimax and higher-order transport theory treats the case in which target and source share the full covariate vector. The continuous strict-subset case is identified but left open because its observed-law functional is cubic.
fill: The project supplies an observable seven-measure reduction, a separate-resolution cubic histogram estimator, a finite-sample variance and cancellation lemma, and a legal sign-mixture lower bound yielding the full rate and the critical elbow.
